lines.trans: I have had enough.
I will not do anything more.
I will tell Eleonora everything myself right now.
Let's celebrate your return, Denis.
What return?
I will not stay here long.
And I thought you would come back for good.
Katya talked to her mom because of you.
Yes, she pleaded for you.
She said, do not meddle in my personal life.
She still loves you, I am telling you for sure.
I do not know, we will see.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: За нашим столиком будет сидеть олигарх.
examples.trans: An oligarch will be sitting at our table.

examples.text: Подождите, у нас столик на четверых.
examples.trans: Wait, our table is for four.
And you end up with six people.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And you end up with six people.

examples.text: Вы у нас директор ресторана, Илья.
examples.trans: You are our restaurant director, Ilya.
And Dmitry Vladimirovich's tailcoat.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'enough', paired with 'хватать'.

examples.trans: I have had enough.
Alright, enough, go and sleep it off.
There wasn't enough money.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Свободного времени у тебя появится очень много.
examples.trans: You will suddenly have plenty of free time.
Sorry, I cannot, there is a lot of work.
Oh my goodness, thank you so much!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Nothing, I am very happy.

examples.text: Но ничто не оправдывает его вранья.
examples.trans: But nothing excuses his lying.
Nothing is working out with Katya.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Make it faster, okay?
What are you doing here?
To make cookies from the family recipe.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You tell me how to do it.
Take it to my suite.

examples.text: Я надеюсь, вам повторять не надо.
examples.trans: I hope I do not need to repeat to you.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will be'.

examples.trans: Maybe he left on his own?
I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'yourself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я читал сам про это дело.
examples.trans: I read about this matter myself.

examples.text: Ты сама взяла и уволила Дениса.
examples.trans: You went ahead and fired Denis yourself.
Maybe he left on his own?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: We will make new cookies right now.

examples.text: Я сам сейчас всё скажу Элеоноре.
examples.trans: I will tell Eleonora everything myself right now.

examples.text: Я понимаю, что сейчас не вовремя.
examples.trans: I understand that now is not the right time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я сам сейчас всё скажу Элеоноре.
examples.trans: I will tell Eleonora everything myself right now.
I understood everything.
Everything's fine.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will say', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Сказала, не лезь в мою личную жизнь.
examples.trans: She said, do not meddle in my personal life.

examples.text: Все, что ты сейчас услышал, ты сам себе сказал.
examples.trans: Everything you just heard, you said to yourself.
What did you say?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

examples.trans: Let's go through the wedding script.

examples.text: Давайте я вам покажу ваш номер.
examples.trans: Let me show you to your suite.
Nikita, let's do it tomorrow.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'метить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to celebrate, to note', paired with 'отмечать'.

examples.trans: Let's celebrate your return, Denis.
But we should celebrate that.
We need to celebrate this.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я виновата, я вмешивалась в твою жизнь.
examples.trans: I am at fault, I interfered in your life.

examples.text: Я никогда больше не буду лезть в твою жизнь.
examples.trans: I will never meddle in your life again.
Well you see, your Denis will be here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'звращение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'return' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Let's celebrate your return, Denis.
What return?
Welcome back!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'which', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You tell me how to do it.

examples.text: У вас ко мне какое-то дело?
examples.trans: Do you have some business with me?
What is her name?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What are you doing here?
You have high staff turnover here.
I will not stay here long.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'держаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will stay long', paired with 'задерживаться'.

examples.trans: I will be delayed at work.
I will also be delayed a bit today.

examples.text: А я шеф, я немного задержусь!
examples.trans: And I am the chef, I will be a little late!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: За нашим столиком будет сидеть олигарх.
examples.trans: An oligarch will be sitting at our table.

examples.text: Подождите, у нас столик на четверых.
examples.trans: Wait, our table is for four.
And you end up with six people.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'thought', paired with 'подумать'.

examples.trans: Come on, do not even think of it!

examples.text: Я уж думала, что ты от меня сбежал.
examples.trans: I already thought that you ran away from me.

examples.text: А я думал, ты навсегда вернёшься.
examples.trans: And I thought you would come back for good.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не знаю, помнишь ты или нет.
examples.trans: I do not know whether you remember or not.
You are fired.
You are fired!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'всегда').

examples.text: А я думал, ты навсегда вернёшься.
examples.trans: And I thought you would come back for good.
Leave this place forever!
They parted forever.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'you come back, will return', paired with 'возвращаться'.

examples.trans: I'll be back soon.
He came back home.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'because of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Катя из-за тебя поговорила с мамой.
examples.trans: Katya talked to her mom because of you.

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!
We were late because of the rain.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Катя из-за тебя поговорила с мамой.
examples.trans: Katya talked to her mom because of you.

examples.text: Но я хотел поговорить про твою маму.
examples.trans: But I wanted to talk about your mom.
Talk to him.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'Mum' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Катя говорила маме, что ты ей очень нравишься.
examples.trans: Katya told her mom that she likes you very much.
Mom, you look gorgeous.

examples.text: Катя из-за тебя поговорила с мамой.
examples.trans: Katya talked to her mom because of you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Yes, alright.
Let's go through the wedding script.
Make it faster, okay?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Замуж она выходит не в моем кабинете.
examples.trans: She is not getting married in my office.

examples.text: Я приехал с супругой, а вот она.
examples.trans: I arrived with my wife, and here she is.
Yes, she pleaded for you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'asked for', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.trans: Yes, she pleaded for you.
I apologise.
He's asking for help.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: За нашим столиком будет сидеть олигарх.
examples.trans: An oligarch will be sitting at our table.
Chef, everyone back to work.
Everyone get to work!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'poke nose, meddle', paired with 'полезть'.

examples.text: Я никогда больше не буду лезть в твою жизнь.
examples.trans: I will never meddle in your life again.

examples.text: Сказала, не лезь в мою личную жизнь.
examples.trans: She said, do not meddle in my personal life.

examples.text: Ладно тебе, я даже болезней таких не знаю.
examples.trans: Come on, I do not even know such illnesses.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They called and will definitely come.

examples.text: Подождите, у нас столик на четверых.
examples.trans: Wait, our table is for four.
And you end up with six people.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh my goodness, thank you so much!
And where is my betrothed?

examples.text: Катя из-за тебя поговорила с мамой.
examples.trans: Katya talked to her mom because of you.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('personal').

examples.text: Это так ты не вмешиваешься в мою личную жизнь?
examples.trans: Is this how you do not interfere in my personal life?

examples.text: Сказала, не лезь в мою личную жизнь.
examples.trans: She said, do not meddle in my personal life.

examples.text: Я хочу предложить вам стать моим личным поваром.
examples.trans: I want to offer you to become my personal chef.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я виновата, я вмешивалась в твою жизнь.
examples.trans: I am at fault, I interfered in your life.

examples.text: Я никогда больше не буду лезть в твою жизнь.
examples.trans: I will never meddle in your life again.

examples.text: Это так ты не вмешиваешься в мою личную жизнь?
examples.trans: Is this how you do not interfere in my personal life?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'loves', paired with 'полюбить'.

examples.text: Она тебя любит еще, я тебе точно говорю.
examples.trans: She still loves you, I am telling you for sure.
She definitely loves you!

examples.text: Тебя никто не любит и не ценит.
examples.trans: Nobody loves you or appreciates you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'still', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You've still got some.
You'll be sorry!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: They called and will definitely come.
Dima, may I have you for a moment?

examples.text: Она тебя любит еще, я тебе точно говорю.
examples.trans: She still loves you, I am telling you for sure.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'speak', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.text: Катя говорила маме, что ты ей очень нравишься.
examples.trans: Katya told her mom that she likes you very much.

examples.text: Я говорила, что я здесь ни при чем.
examples.trans: I told you that I had nothing to do with it.

examples.text: Катя из-за тебя поговорила с мамой.
examples.trans: Katya talked to her mom because of you.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'know'.

examples.text: Не знаю, помнишь ты или нет.
examples.trans: I do not know whether you remember or not.

examples.text: Ты прекрасно знаешь, что мы расстались.
examples.trans: You know very well that we broke up.
I do not know, we will see.

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'we shall see', paired with 'смотреть'.

examples.trans: May I have a look?
I only had a look.
Can I go and have a look?
